title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. E is an elliptic curve over k (char ≠ 2) in the form y² = f(z) = z³ + a₁z² + a₂z + a₃ = (z−ζ_i)(z−ζ_λ)(z−ζ_μ). The three nonzero 2‑torsion points are ε_i = (ζ_i, 0), indexed by the 3‑element set J = ₂E(k)*. Coordinates are z = ℘, z' = ℘' (normalised via a chosen δ ∈ t_E* and an associated ℘ ∈ 𝒯₂).

The data. Grothendieck considers what the previous page calls a 'relative Jacobi épinglage of level 4': a family (x_i), with x_i ∈ E(k), 2x_i = ε_i and Σ x_i = 0. Each x_i is a 4‑torsion point halving ε_i.

The system (71). In coordinates z_i = ℘(x_i), z'_i = ℘'(x_i) the data become three conditions:
- Halving condition. 2x = ε_i forces (z_i − ζ_i)² = f'(ζ_i) = (ζ_i−ζ_λ)(ζ_i−ζ_μ). This is the classical halving formula x(P) = e_i ± √((e_i−e_j)(e_i−e_k)). Grothendieck rewrites it using f(ζ_i) = 0 as −(1/ζ_i)(a₁ζ_i² + 2a₂ζ_i + 3a₃), and in the margin as a linear relation for z_i².
- Curve equation. z'_i² = f(z_i) puts the point on the curve.
- Collinearity. The three points (z_i, z'_i) are collinear: det[1, z_i, z'_i] = 0. This is equivalent to x₁ + x₂ + x₃ = 0 because the x_i are distinct and nonzero.

The determinant expands as ψ₁ + ψ₂ + ψ₃ = 0, with ψ_i^ω = z_j z'_k − z_k z'_j for (i, j, k) cyclic under a circular order ω on J. Reversing ω changes every ψ by a sign, so the condition is orientation‑independent.

Count. There are 2 choices of z_i and 2 of z'_i, so the indeterminacy of x_i is a ₂E(k)‑torsor, as it must be.

Programme announced. From such level‑4 data, Grothendieck wants to produce computationally, via (71), a 'Legendre épi‑flag' of E. The construction is to be functorial in E and compatible with the 'diagramme fondamental' (defined elsewhere in the notes). He first fixes a primitive fourth root of unity i ∈ μ₄*(k). Then:
- The first datum α of a Legendre épi‑flag becomes a circular order ω on J (α = i ∧ ω).
- The second datum K becomes an isomorphism t_E ≃ O_{Σ_J,t}(1) = O_t(1). Here Σ_J is the canonical projective line attached to the 3‑element set J (the Legendre λ‑line with the three marked points J), and t is the point of Σ_J corresponding to E.

The next page fixes K by requiring that K^{⊗2} match the canonical isomorphisms t_E^{⊗2} ≃ T_{Σ_J,t} ≃ O_t(2)(ω), where (ω) denotes the orientation twist. The first of these is the Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism for the Legendre family; the second comes from the Euler sequence 0 → F_t → V_J → O_t(1) → 0.

So a Legendre épi‑flag is an orientation of J together with a square root of the Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism, i.e. a trivialisation t_E ≅ O(1) at t. This is determined up to μ₄, or up to sign once α is fixed. The page sets up the algebra by which level‑4 'Jacobi' data are to pin down this square root, which is classically the passage from Legendre's λ to Jacobi's modulus k with λ = k².
errors: The bracketed simplification of the first line of (71) has a sign slip. Using a₃ = −ζ_iζ_λζ_μ, one gets −(1/ζ_i)(a₁ζ_i² + 2a₂ζ_i + 3a₃) = −a₁ζ_i − 2a₂ + 3ζ_λζ_μ = (ζ_i−ζ_λ)(ζ_i−ζ_μ). The bracket should therefore read −(a₁ζ_i + 2a₂ − 3ζ_λζ_μ), not −(a₁ζ_i + 2a₂ + 3ζ_λζ_μ).
The marginal relation carries the same sign slip. Correctly it is z_i² = 2ζ_i z_i − (a₂ − 2ζ_λζ_μ), not −(a₂ + 2ζ_λζ_μ).
The form −(1/ζ_i)(…) presupposes ζ_i ≠ 0. This is harmless, since the bracketed form or f'(ζ_i) avoids the division.

Minor point: the determinant criterion for Σx_i = 0 needs the three points distinct and none at the origin. Both hold because the 2x_i are the distinct nonzero ε_i, as Grothendieck notes on the previous page.

ideas.what: Coordinates of halves of 2‑torsion points: (℘(x) − e_i)² = (e_i−e_j)(e_i−e_k) when 2x = ε_i, with the ℘' choice giving the ₂E torsor
ideas.modern_name: 4‑division / halving formulas on a Weierstrass cubic
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Jacobi, Weierstrass); standard in Silverman, Husemöller

ideas.what: Collinearity determinant expressing x₁ + x₂ + x₃ = 0, written as a cyclic sum ψ₁ + ψ₂ + ψ₃ depending on a circular order only up to sign
ideas.modern_name: group law via the chord construction

ideas.what: Level‑4 'relative Jacobi épinglage': halves x_i of the three 2‑torsion points with Σx_i = 0
ideas.modern_name: a (partial) Γ(4)‑type level structure refining full level 2; the Jacobi modulus k with λ = k²
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical Jacobi/Legendre theory; moduli formulation in Deligne–Rapoport, Katz–Mazur

ideas.what: Legendre épi‑flag: an orientation of J = ₂E* (using a chosen i ∈ μ₄*) plus an isomorphism t_E ≅ O_t(1) on the canonical P¹ Σ_J whose square is the Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism t_E^{⊗2} ≅ T_{Σ_J,t}
ideas.modern_name: square root of the Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism ω^{⊗2} ≅ Ω¹(log cusps) on the λ‑line; Hodge bundle as a 'theta characteristic' of the modular curve
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism for modular curves: Deligne, Katz (1970s); Legendre family: classical

ideas.what: Canonical P¹ Σ_J attached to a 3‑element set J, with the Euler sequence and orientation twist O_t(2)(ω) ≅ T_{Σ_J,t} (developed on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: P(V_J) with V_J = functions on J summing to zero; det V_J = orientation line

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets out to build, functorially in E and compatibly with his 'fundamental diagram', a map from level‑4 Jacobi data (halves of 2‑torsion points summing to zero) to square roots of the Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism on the canonical λ‑line attached to ₂E*. This makes intrinsic and coordinate‑free the classical fact that Jacobi's k = √λ trivialises the Hodge bundle up to μ₄. The page gives only the equations and the programme, not the construction.
missed.quote: Je voudrais, à une telle donnée₂ (x_i)_{i∈I}, exprimer calculatoirement … associer un épi-flag de Legendre de E, de façon fonctorielle en E et compatible avec le diagramme fondamental
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a canonical, choice‑free description of the Hodge bundle on the level‑2 and level‑4 moduli stacks as a square root of the log tangent bundle on the canonical P¹ of a 3‑set. It is mildly interesting for stacky treatments of half‑integral weight / spin structures on modular curves, but probably recoverable from the known theory (Katz–Mazur, theta multiplier) by specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: The explicit algebra is classical, and the page contains two sign slips. The only somewhat distinctive element is the conceptual framing: a 'Legendre épi‑flag' as an orientation plus a square root of the Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism, to be induced functorially from level‑4 Jacobi data. It is an unfinished programme rather than a result, and its content is close to known facts about ω² ≅ Ω¹(log) on modular curves.
transcription_corrections: Margin: it reads z_i² = 2ζ_i z_i − (a₂ + 2ζ_λζ_μ) (an expression for z_i², not z'_i²). Mathematically the index should be ζ_i, and the sign inside should be −2ζ_λζ_μ.
Line (75): the image shows J = ₂E(k)* = {ε_i} and ω ∈ ω̲ = ω̲_J (index J, not I).

Line (76): the target is O_{Σ_J,t}(1) (index J). The superscript read as '⊗5' is doubtful; the arrow to O_t(1) is annotated with the circled insertion 'grâce au choix de i' (thanks to the choice of i).
'conjointement' is an insertion written above 'associés' in the phrase 'via le choix d'un δ ∈ t_E* et ℘ ∈ 𝒯₂ (conjointement) associés'.
